items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: the band was smaller than Les Hite's band, and Elkins was -- well, he was not the musician that Les Hite was... until Les Hite came.

ctx.x: Interview with Lawrence Brown. This is July 3rd, 1976. Lawrence, I was reading in Max Jones' and John Chilton's book on Louis Armstrong that the band at the Cotton Club was led by a trumpet player named Vernon Elkins until Les Hite took over. Tell me a little bit about the band then.

Well, the band was smaller than Les Hite's band, and Elkins was -- well, he was not the musician that Les Hite was, and so therefore it wasn't up to par, we would say, and the greatest thing about the band at that time was when Louie, in 1930, came out as a solo artist and naturally he fronted the band, and from then on, why it was a different band in that the arrangements were better and the solos were more interesting and it was just a better organization, until Les Hite came.
And then he was a better musician, or more used to arranging and framing up the bands. He sang and he was more of a leader. That's when the band became very nice, we'd call it.
